reading.body:
The only hard output this record contains is a single granted US patent, issued November 11, 2025, for training a sentiment preference recognition model on comment information.

That is the whole of the measurable evidence. A government lab in Beijing, non-profit, known as BAAI and associated with the alias WuDao, holds one granted US patent in the USPTO dataset covering grants since 2001. The patent is a machine learning training and recognition method, which places the organization's documented US intellectual property in applied natural language processing rather than in the compute, power, or data center layer that constrains AI scaling.

The record does not list products, so there is no way to trace what the research produced or whether it was deployed. It records no lawsuits. It says nothing about the organization's compute footprint, its power arrangements, or the buildings it operates in, and nothing in the data supports an inference about any of them. The profile text is the organization's own description of itself, including its stated focus on policy, academic thought, theoretical foundations, talent, and the industrial ecosystem, and should be read as a self-description rather than a verified finding.

What the data cannot answer is scale. One patent and an empty product list do not distinguish a large research institution from a small one, and the absence of lawsuits and products reflects what this particular dataset collects, not what exists.

profile_text.body:
The Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence describes itself on its site as a new-type research institution in the field of artificial intelligence. It says it brings together leading international AI scholars and focuses on core technology and original innovation. Its stated aim is to advance what it calls five sources of innovation: policy, academic thought, theoretical foundations, top talent, and the industrial ecosystem.

The organization is also known as BAAI, and the alias WuDao is associated with it. It is a non-profit government lab headquartered in Beijing, China. No lawsuits involving the organization are recorded, and no products are listed under its name.
